title: Suspension equivalence between the boundary RGB poset and non-simple disc complex
difficulty_reason: The proof identifies the intersection of two contractible colour-defined subposets with the non-simple-disc poset via Quillen fibre lemma. Its source-specific fibre argument recolours discs through a deflating map followed by two inflating maps and identifies the image with simple disc systems in the cut handlebody; the separate author proof that both subposets are contractible is included. The resulting suspension equivalence is a distinct assertion from the virtual duality and dualizing module conclusion of existing 2386; its complete proof is also part of the latter’s author proof and is not treated as an unproved background assumption. Quillen fibre lemma and the contractibility theorem are attributed standard inputs.

proof_spans.label: Poset lemmas, cited disc-complex contractibility, full author colour-forgetting contraction and proof of Theorem 4.1

context_spans.label: Essential disc systems and non-simple disc complex

readability.basis: Existing 17-page reader from batch-14872-14875-r004; physically viewed pages 9, 11 and 12 including statement, colour-forgetting contractions and proof conclusion.

dedup.scope: Current master titles searched for handlebody, disc complex, disk complex and disc system; tex body searched for conjunction non-simple and handlebody. Same fixed work 2386 and selected theorem A/C compared.

compared.relation: Existing entry selects virtual duality and identification of a dualizing module for unmarked handlebodies of genus at least two. The present original Theorem 4.1 is a geometric homotopy equivalence for genus greater than zero with marked settings as in the authors’ definitions; it is explicitly a substantial dependency of 2386, not an alternate proof of the same proposition.
